facts.statement: Rhamphodopsis lived during the Middle Devonian period.
The genus Rhamphodopsis was described by Watson in 1934.
Rhamphodopsis is classified as an extinct ptyctodont placoderm.
facts.quote: Rhamphodopsis is a genus of extinct ptyctodont placoderm

facts.statement: Fossils of Rhamphodopsis have been found in the Middle Devonian Old Red Sandstone of Scotland.
facts.quote: from the Middle Devonian Old Red Sandstone of Scotland

facts.statement: The type species Rhamphodopsis thrieplandi grew to a maximum adult length of 7 centimeters.
facts.quote: the adult total length being up to 7 centimeters

facts.statement: The species Rhamphodopsis trispinatus reached an adult total length of up to 12 centimeters.
facts.quote: the adult total length being up to 12 centimeters

facts.statement: Rhamphodopsis trispinatus is distinguished by having median dorsal and anterior lateral spines of proportionally equal lengths.
facts.quote: the median dorsal and anterior lateral spines of R. trispinatus are both proportionally equal lengths

facts.statement: Rhamphodopsis belongs to the parent group Ptyctodontida.
Rhamphodopsis is classified within the class Placodermi.
The time range for Rhamphodopsis is the Eifelian stage, from 393.47 to 387.95 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Eifelian to Eifelian (393.47 to 387.95 million years ago)
